transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon, Mr. Potter! A pleasure to see you. Back for a new set of polish, perhaps, or eyeing up the latest Nimbus? What can Quality Quidditch Supplies do for you today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I...I actually came to return the broom-servicing kit I bought a few days ago. There seems to be an issue with it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, a return, you say? Hmm. Let me see the kit, Mr. Potter. Though, I must inform you that all servicing kits are non-refundable once the seal is broken, Mr. Potter. You'll have to take it up with the manufacturer directly — that's a six-week owl exchange minimum, I'm afraid. Is the seal broken on this one?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Er...I...I can't remember, sir. It's possible it is, but I only opened it to use it and found it wasn't working properly. The handle polish is dry and the clippers are rusted. It's...it's not in a condition that I can use. I don't think that's right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, Puddifoot and Sons, you say? Hmm. Well, Mr. Potter, I do sympathise entirely – it's certainly not what one expects from a brand like that. However, as I mentioned, once a servicing kit is opened and used, even once, we simply cannot take it back here at Quality Quidditch Supplies. It's a standard policy for consumables and tools, you understand.

Your issue with the dry polish and rusted clippers is definitely something to take up with Puddifoot and Sons directly. They're usually quite good about honouring their quality, but the exchange process for a faulty item *through them* is the proper channel. You'll want to send them an owl outlining the problem, and they'll arrange a replacement. Do you still have the packaging with their address?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I...I don't have the packaging anymore. I just...I wasn't expecting it to be faulty. I mean, it's a reputable brand, right? I thought it would be fine. I don't even have the receipt...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Oh, no receipt and no packaging? That certainly complicates matters for a direct manufacturer exchange, Mr. Potter. I do understand your frustration completely; it's a nuisance when things don't work as they should, especially from a brand you trust.

However, our policy stands firm on opened servicing kits. Once that seal is broken, we can't verify the contents or their condition upon leaving the store, you see. It becomes a matter for Puddifoot and Sons to rectify.

Even without the original packaging, you could still try sending an owl to Puddifoot and Sons directly. They're based in Hogsmeade – you could address it to 'Puddifoot and Sons, Broom Care Division, Hogsmeade'. Explain the situation clearly, detailing the dry polish and rusted clippers, and mention when you purchased it, even without the exact date. They *might* be able to help, though it's not a guarantee without proof of purchase.

Is there anything else I can assist you with today, perhaps some fresh handle polish from a different brand, or a new set of clippers individually, to tide you over?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I...I don't know, sir. This is just...frustrating. I bought this to fix my broom and now it's not even usable. I don't have the receipt or the packaging...I don't even know where to start with this. It's just...disappointing.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I completely understand, Mr. Potter, it's a truly frustrating situation to be in when you're looking to get your broom in top condition and hit a snag like this. It's perfectly natural to be disappointed.

As much as I wish I could simply swap it out for you right here, our hands are tied with opened servicing kits, especially without the receipt or packaging to confirm the purchase details from our end. It puts us in a very difficult position.

However, I strongly recommend still sending that owl to Puddifoot and Sons. They *do* have a reputation to uphold, and sometimes, for exceptional circumstances, they might make an exception. You could even mention that you purchased it from Quality Quidditch Supplies – sometimes that can help. Their address again is 'Puddifoot and Sons, Broom Care Division, Hogsmeade.' Just explain what happened clearly.

Perhaps, in the meantime, if you only need the handle polish and clippers urgently, we could look at individual items? We have a new batch of Nimbus 'Glide-Smooth' polish that's very popular, and some excellent rust-proof bronze clippers. I could even offer you a small discount on those, given your current predicament, to help you get back in the air quicker?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I...I don't know, sir. This is...a lot. I mean, I came in here to get my broom fixed, and now I'm stuck with a broken kit and no idea what to do next. I just...I don't want to deal with all this. I don't have time to send owls and wait for responses...I need to practice! My next match is in...I don't even have time to think about this!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I truly, truly understand, Mr. Potter. A Quidditch match looming means every minute counts, and this sort of unexpected hassle is the last thing you need. It's completely understandable that you're feeling overwhelmed and frustrated; your focus should be on practice, not on faulty equipment or owl post.

While I simply cannot take back the opened kit for a refund, my main concern is getting you match-ready. If time is of the essence, as it clearly is, sending an owl to Puddifoot and Sons might indeed take too long for your immediate needs.

Perhaps the most efficient solution to get your broom in top shape *today* would be to pick up those individual items you absolutely need. We have the Nimbus 'Glide-Smooth' handle polish right here – it's excellent, dries quickly, and is very durable. And our bronze clippers are famously rust-resistant. As I said, I'd be happy to give you that discount on them to help ease the burden. It would mean you could sort your broom out this afternoon and get back to practice without further delay.

What do you think? It's not ideal, I know, but it gets you back on your broom quicker than anything else.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You're right...I need to get back to practice. If you can give me a discount on the polish and clippers, that would be...great. I mean, it's not what I wanted, but it's better than nothing. I just want to get my broom fixed and...fly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Excellent, Mr. Potter, that's the spirit! Sometimes the quickest solution is the best one, especially when a Quidditch match is on the horizon. We'll get you sorted out immediately so you can get back to what you do best.

Right then, for you, I'll take 15% off the Nimbus 'Glide-Smooth' polish and a brand new pair of our best rust-proof bronze clippers. That should certainly get your broom gleaming and performing perfectly.

If you'll just follow me this way, I'll fetch those for you from the display. You won't regret these; they're top-notch. And rest assured, we'll make sure they're in perfect condition before they leave the shop.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. I appreciate you helping me out like this. I'll...I'll get my broom fixed and get back to flying. I really need to focus on my practice.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
My pleasure, Mr. Potter, truly. It's the least we can do to ensure a champion like yourself isn't grounded by faulty equipment. That's what Quality Quidditch Supplies is here for – to get you back in the air, soaring high.

These new items will serve you wonderfully, I assure you. You'll be back to your practice in no time, and your Firebolt will feel like new. Now, let's get you over to the counter and we'll have these polished and clipped items wrapped up for you. Follow me right this way.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right, thank you. I'm sorry for the...trouble. I didn't mean to cause any issues. I'll be sure to recommend Quality Quidditch Supplies to...well, anyone who asks. You've been very...helpful.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
No trouble at all, Mr. Potter, not in the slightest! That's what we're here for – to assist our valued customers, especially when things go awry. We always appreciate your custom, and a recommendation from you is as good as gold.

Don't you worry about a thing; consider it sorted. Your focus should be entirely on your practice now. Here are your new items – the Nimbus polish and those sturdy clippers. They're all ready for you. Just at the counter here, please.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I...I really appreciate your help, Mr. Zonko. I'll get these items and...get out of your way. I have a lot of work to do, so...I'm off. Thank you again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
It's Mr. *Sparks*, actually, but you are most welcome, Mr. Potter! Happy to be of service. We're always here if you need anything else for your broom.

Go on now, get that broom spick and span and show them what you're made of! Best of luck with your practice and your upcoming match! Come back and tell us how it went!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right, of course, Mr. Sparks. I'm...I'm sorry for the mix-up. I'll...I'll tell everyone about your store. I hope...I hope to see you again, under...better circumstances. Thank you again.
